correctness.rationale: The proof is complete for every \(n\ge6\). Any even \(a\) in \(\{6,8,\ldots,2n-4\}\) yields one of two explicit four-tuples whose non-\(a\) pair sums are odd and within the interval, forcing every safe triple into four boundary values. Three boundary triples are then eliminated by two explicit uniform witnesses. For the surviving triple, a parity split shows that three same-parity summands are impossible; under a two-two split the two larger opposite-parity summands are each at least \(n\), so their cross-sum exceeds \(2n\). All distinctness and endpoint inequalities are checked in the proof. Finite enumeration is supplementary only.
